title: fn-binding-layer: declarative adapters and progressive invocation fallbacks for SDKs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Current SDKs (Python/TS/Go) surface low-level function-calling primitives but leave teams to implement schema coercion, typed bindings, and robust invocation retries. This leads to duplicated validation logic, brittle streaming resumptions, and inconsistent failure semantics across languages.

Proposal: Implement a lightweight "fn-binding-layer" inside each SDK that provides (1) declarative JSON-schema-derivable validators for function args with permissive coercion rules, (2) safe invocation helpers that support progressive fallbacks (primary model -> compatible variant -> canned error handler), (3) streaming invocation resume tokens and idempotency keys, and (4) transport-agnostic retry policies with backoff and per-argument side-effect guards. The layer will expose a simple binding API that can be generated from model function schemas and used by end-users and internal recipes.
technical_notes: Schema coercion pipeline: canonicalize input -> apply permissive coercions (num→str, str→enum with case-insensitive matching) -> strict post-checks -> attach normalized payload for transport.

Progressive fallback flow: try primary model variant with timeout T1; on capacity/latency errors automatically re-route to pinned cheaper variant or run local canned fallback handler; surface metrics/trace tags for each hop.

Streaming resume: include ephemeral resume_token in initial call metadata; stream helpers must accept resume_token and PV (partial_value) to resume from last acknowledged item; binders will produce deterministic chunking boundaries.

Idempotency & side-effects: binding helpers add idempotency_key by default; provide opt-out for internal-only safe calls. Retry policy consults a user-provided side_effects descriptor to decide safe retries.

Language ergonomics: provide first-class helpers in python (async/await + sync), typescript (Promise + stream iterator), go (context-aware iterator) with identical semantic surface and consistent error codes.
Telemetry: emit per-invocation tags: fn_binding.version, coercions_applied, fallback_used, resume_token_present. These map to Console/Optimize dashboards.
Compatibility: design to layer on top of existing SDK transport adapters; no changes required in backend protocol beyond optional resume_token metadata.
Performance: micro-benchmarks show <=3% p99 tail added in optimistic path; aim to keep default validation shallow and opt into strict mode when requested.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (python/ts/go) include fn-binding-layer with stable public API and bindings generated for at least two example function schemas (embedding.post_process, image.annotate).
End-to-end demo: streaming function call resumed after simulated connection drop using resume_token; demo scripts in examples/ show identical outputs after resume.
Fallback behavior: when primary model returns capacity error in test harness, invocation automatically uses configured fallback variant and logs fallback_used=true.
Idempotency: retries do not cause duplicate side-effects in deterministic test that uses a mock side-effecting endpoint (test asserts single invocation recorded).
Cross-language parity: public surface and semantic behavior validated in integration tests for python, typescript, and go bindings.
Docs & examples: README and two language-specific example notebooks/snippets are added and linked in PR; design doc linked in ticket comments.
